title: Larger models: upward Löwenheim–Skolem and model sizes
summary: Build large elementary extensions, obtain models of every sufficiently large infinite size, and distinguish size changes from independence witnesses.
abstract: A first-order theory can specify a finite number of elements. Once it has an infinite model, it has models of arbitrarily large cardinality. By adding names for distinct elements, we can enlarge any infinite structure while preserving every formula about its original elements. Combining this construction with smaller elementary submodels gives models of every infinite cardinality at least as large as the language. Requiring an extension of a particular structure adds one more restriction: the new domain must be large enough to contain the old one. These changes in size preserve sentences, so they do not by themselves show that a sentence is independent of the axioms. Independence instead requires models in which that sentence has different truth values.
